searchText: **nrryuya** (in reply to **vbuterin**) Yeah, to randomize the timing of attestations would somewhat mitigate the probability of successful splitting. I think this is one of the challenges to prove the liveness of ETH2.0 since we need a network model which capture the unpredictability of gossipping network, which is stronger than the traditional one where only the upper bound of message delay is assumed. Also, we should analyze how much extent adversary can predict splitting by observing and experimenting with the network. **nrryuya** BTW, when it comes to the incentive-compatibility of the timing of attestations, I think there is a trade-off between the reward for attesting the main chain (which prevents bribing to vote for a fork-chain, etc.) and the time during which attestors intentionally wait and observe which chain other attestations vote for after the time they originally should publish attestations in order to increase the probability that their attestations end up in the main chain even though the reduction of the reward based on inclusion delay increases. 0.8.2 tests don't have bls test cases anymore? <mratsim> https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/tree/dev/test_generators/bls ? <mratsim> but yeah it seems like they are missing from the tests repo <mratsim> there are plenty of shuffling tests now though **protolambda** They moved to a general folder I cannot find them there, only ssz-generic **protolambda** Hmm, yes, looks like they didn't run though **protolambda** Will run them, along with that small ssz test improvement, and push them to branch. Sorry about that, nothing really breaking however. **protolambda** But yes, probably a good idea to run those tests now that BLS domain bytes are passed correctly Here is a revision with the BLS test vectors, and a correction for nil-mode randomization not being completely nil: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-spec-tests/pull/11 <@545555441518772225> @schroedingerscode <@456226577798135808> It will get pulled into a smaller testing release, or v0.8.3, when Danny is back. Is there a such thing as an empty ssz vector? Or is it assumed to be zero initialized (or something similar)? vectors will just be zeroed by default or zeroed instances of the element type. Can be composite. > vectors will just be zeroed by default Is this in the SSZ spec? Can't seem to locate it they are called "default values" Under here? https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/simple-serialize.md#default-values yes, "recursively defined". Probably to lean as definition... If you like it to be more explicit, we welcome a PR 😃 haha great, I'll do that. Us small minded folk need that sometimes 😄 Totally agree that the spec is too "minimal" in some ways. Finding the right balance is hard though **schroedingerscode** While I'm quite familiar with the recursive definition nature of the SSZ spec, Matt actually makes a good point about vectors being ambiguous. The spec reads: `Default values The default value of a type upon initialization is recursively defined using 0 for uintN, False for boolean and the elements of Bitvector, and [] for lists and Bitlist. Unions default to the first type in the union (with type index zero), which is null if present in the union.` And while it might be kind of implicit that a default vector of SSZ types is just N number of the default values for the containing type, it does seem suspiciously absent from the above default values definition, which mentions the SSZ primitives, as well as Bitvector, Bitlist, Lists, and Unions. Poor vector just feels left out. **schroedingerscode** **mattgarnett** - I can make a PR explicitly adding vector to the above definition, unless you'd like to/already have. Don't want to steal your thunder. I welcome a PR that is explicit about the default values, per type. I put a PR in earlier after our conversation 😃 https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/1346

excerpts.content: Yeah, to randomize the timing of attestations would somewhat mitigate the probability of successful splitting. I think this is one of the challenges to prove the liveness of ETH2.0 since we need a network model which capture the unpredictability of gossipping network, which is stronger than the traditional one where only the upper bound of message delay is assumed. Also, we should analyze how much extent adversary can predict splitting by observing and experimenting with the network.

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**nrryuya**
BTW, when it comes to the incentive-compatibility of the timing of attestations, I think there is a trade-off between the reward for attesting the main chain (which prevents bribing to vote for a fork-chain, etc.) and the time during which attestors intentionally wait and observe which chain other attestations vote for after the time they originally should publish attestations in order to increase the probability that their attestations end up in the main chain even though the reduction of the reward based on inclusion delay increases.

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**schroedingerscode**
While I'm quite familiar with the recursive definition nature of the SSZ spec, Matt actually makes a good point about vectors being ambiguous. The spec reads:

`Default values
The default value of a type upon initialization is recursively defined using 0 for uintN, False for boolean and the elements of Bitvector, and [] for lists and Bitlist. Unions default to the first type in the union (with type index zero), which is null if present in the union.`

And while it might be kind of implicit that a default vector of SSZ types is just N number of the default values for the containing type, it does seem suspiciously absent from the above default values definition, which mentions the SSZ primitives, as well as Bitvector, Bitlist, Lists, and Unions. Poor vector just feels left out.
